claims.head: Who drives the play: the Canadiens
claims.body: The Canadiens have been around the middle of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. TOR.head: A slightly uphill night for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

MTL.head: The Canadiens have a slight edge
MTL.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can still swing it if their power play gets going.

story.head: Open season on the Maple Leafs’ net
paras: The Canadiens already played in Toronto once this season and left with a 3-2 win on Sep 29. The Canadiens (10-3-3) beat Utah 5-4 in overtime on Thursday, while the Maple Leafs (8-7-2) lost 3-2 to Utah on Tuesday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Canadiens second (sixth in the NHL) and the Maple Leafs seventh (19th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Canadiens’ record (.719) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely because they’re 7-4 in one-goal games. So is the Maple Leafs’ (.529 on chances worth .478), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Canadiens (32nd) and the Maple Leafs (31st) both take more penalties than they draw. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than anyone (1st) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (27th). The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Habs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. Beyond that, the Canadiens roll four lines, but the Maple Leafs lean on their top six.

Lane Hutson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, and Cole Caufield (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. Auston Matthews (11 G / 15 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and six goals in ten games against Montréal since 2023-24. William Nylander (10 G / 11 A / 21 P in 17 GP) is next in line.
Jacob Fowler (7-1-1 / .925 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and is expected to start. Sergei Bobrovsky (3-6-2 / .889 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for Toronto.
The Canadiens usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Josh Anderson, and have been without Ivan Demidov, Samuel Montembeault and Mike Matheson for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko, have been without Nick Blankenburg since Oct 22, and have had to make do without Max Domi all season.
John Tavares has missed the Maple Leafs’ last nine games.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 5.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
